report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of 5 of daedalus/council/vendors.py: floor_check, _withheld_paths, council_env, council_cwd, run_managed, CouncilProfile, COUNCIL_PROFILES, _assert_profile_safe, CouncilAdapter class start; claims verified against code.
risks: floor_check | medium | evidence_paths only checks path channel; value-shaped regexes are not run on the path itself, and if a secret is embedded in a filename (e.g., 'config/id_rsa') it would not be caught by the path channel unless the rule matches path markers; the docstring implies both channels per path, but code only calls secret_floor_rule(path, "") for paths. | Check secret_floor_rule semantics for path-only checks.

council_cwd | medium | The check `root in here.parents` may be True when here is a sibling of root? Actually `root in here.parents` means root is an ancestor of here, so it correctly detects if temp dir is inside repo root. But if repo_root is a symlink, resolve() is used, so it's fine. No risk.

run_managed | high | The timeout loop uses `proc.returncode` after cancel; if cancel does not set returncode (e.g., process still running), `code` could be None, and RunResult gets returncode=None, which may be misinterpreted. The code sets `code = proc.returncode` without checking if it's None; if cancel is asynchronous, this could be None. | Verify ManagedProcess.cancel() guarantees returncode is set.

council_env | low | Docstring says 'Never set, never mutated, never inherited' but the function returns a copy of os.environ with OLLAMA_HOST popped; it does not prevent the caller from mutating the returned dict or passing it to a subprocess. The claim 'never inherited' is about OLLAMA_HOST not being inherited, which is true. No risk.

council_cwd | medium | The docstring says 'Raises if the system temp dir somehow sits under repo_root' – the code raises if the created temp dir is inside repo_root, not if the system temp dir is. It checks the actual temp dir location, which is more precise. No risk.

run_managed | high | The docstring claims 'The whole process TREE dies on timeout' but the code only calls proc.cancel(); whether that kills the tree depends on ManagedProcess implementation. If cancel only terminates the immediate child, the claim is broken. | Inspect ManagedProcess.cancel().

CouncilProfile | low | The docstring says 'stdin_prompt is always true here and the shape is enforced by test' – but the dataclass allows stdin_prompt=False; the enforcement is by test, not by type. No risk.

COUNCIL_PROFILES | low | The comment says 'tools denied' for anthropic but the profile uses --disallowed-tools, which is correct. For openai, the comment says 'read-only sandbox + approvals never' – codex exec --sandbox read-only --ask-for-approval never, correct. No risk.

_assert_profile_safe | medium | The check uses substring matching on the joined command+args. A flag like '--dontAsk' would be caught, but a flag like '--dontAskMe' would also be caught, which is overly broad but safe. No risk.

handoff.purpose: Verify claims in docstrings/comments of floor_check, _withheld_paths, council_env, council_cwd, run_managed, CouncilProfile, COUNCIL_PROFILES, _assert_profile_safe, and CouncilAdapter class intro.

symbols.name: floor_check
symbols.note: Runs secret floor on evidence paths, evidence files, and prompt; returns FloorRefusal or None.

symbols.name: _withheld_paths
symbols.note: Returns tuple of paths withheld by slice_egress_rule for untrusted lanes.

symbols.name: council_env
symbols.note: Returns environment dict with OLLAMA_HOST removed.

symbols.name: council_cwd
symbols.note: Creates a temporary directory, raises if inside repo_root.

symbols.name: run_managed
symbols.note: Spawns a ManagedProcess with stdin from a temp file, kills tree on timeout, returns RunResult.

symbols.name: Runner
symbols.note: Type alias for callable returning RunResult.

symbols.name: CouncilProfile
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass describing a vendor CLI invocation; stdin_prompt always True.

symbols.name: _CLAUDE_DENIED_TOOLS
symbols.note: String of denied tools for Claude.

symbols.name: COUNCIL_PROFILES
symbols.note: Dict of vendor profiles for anthropic and openai.

symbols.name: CouncilAdapter
symbols.note: Base adapter class; subclasses implement _dispatch; ask is the only entry point.

claims.text: Run the secret floor before anything leaves the process.
claims.why: floor_check is called and returns a FloorRefusal before any I/O in the function; it is the first thing in the function.

claims.text: ``sensitivity.secret_floor_rule`` has two INDEPENDENT channels: path markers checked against ``path``, value-shaped regexes checked against ``text``.
claims.why: The code calls secret_floor_rule(path, "") for paths and secret_floor_rule(path, text) for files, and secret_floor_rule("", prompt) for prompt, matching the two-channel description.

claims.text: the tempting ``secret_floor_rule("", prompt)`` kills the path tier outright: a patch that ADDS ``.env`` or ``config/id_rsa`` sails through, because the only trace of the filename is ``diff --git a/.env b/.env`` inside ``text``, which no content regex matches.
claims.why: The code does not use secret_floor_rule("", prompt) as the only check; it separately checks evidence_paths and evidence_files with the path argument.

claims.text: ``evidence_paths`` -- every changed path (``PatchArtifact.changed_paths``) and every evidence file path, each through the PATH channel alone;
claims.why: The loop `for path in evidence_paths: rule = secret_floor_rule(path, "")` passes the path and empty text, which is the PATH channel alone.

claims.text: ``evidence_files`` -- ``(path, text)`` pairs, both channels, per file;
claims.why: The loop `for path, text in evidence_files: rule = secret_floor_rule(path, text or "")` passes both path and text, so both channels are used.

claims.text: ``prompt`` -- a content-channel BACKSTOP for a credential pasted into the question itself.  It is a backstop, never the whole check.
claims.why: The prompt check is the last check, after evidence_paths and evidence_files, so it is a backstop.

claims.text: Returns the first :class:`FloorRefusal`, or ``None``.  A hit means REFUSE -- there is no redact-and-send.
claims.why: The function returns the first FloorRefusal encountered, otherwise None.

claims.text: Not a decision made by a default argument: an untrusted lane means OpenAI / Google get the allow-list, and every withheld path is named on the reply so a reader can see what the council did NOT see.
claims.why: The function returns () for trusted lane, and for untrusted lanes it computes withheld paths using slice_egress_rule; the reply naming is not in this chunk but the function returns the list.

claims.text: Environment for a council subprocess, with ``OLLAMA_HOST`` STRIPPED.
claims.why: The function copies the base environment and pops OLLAMA_HOST.

claims.text: Never set, never mutated, never inherited -- see the module docstring.
claims.why: The function does not set OLLAMA_HOST, does not mutate the input base (it copies), and the returned dict does not contain OLLAMA_HOST, so it is not inherited by subprocesses.

claims.text: A council that normalises a remote Ollama into a shared environment silently invalidates ``offload.py``'s trusted-lane justification repo-wide.
claims.why: This claim refers to offload.py and repo-wide implications outside this chunk.

claims.text: A fresh, EMPTY temp directory to spawn a council subprocess in.
claims.why: The function creates a TemporaryDirectory with prefix 'dcouncil-cwd-', which is empty and fresh.

claims.text: Not the repo, not a worktree, containing no repo files.
claims.why: The temp directory is created by tempfile.TemporaryDirectory, which is empty and not the repo.

claims.text: Returned as a context manager so the directory is fresh per call and removed after.
claims.why: The function returns a TemporaryDirectory object which is a context manager and cleans up on exit.

claims.text: Raises if the system temp dir somehow sits under ``repo_root``, because a reviewer rooted in the checkout is the failure this exists to prevent.
claims.why: The code checks if the created temp dir is inside repo_root and raises ValueError if so.

claims.text: Default runner: spawn ``argv`` under :class:`spine.cancel.ManagedProcess`.
claims.why: The function uses ManagedProcess(argv, cwd=cwd, env=env, ...).

claims.text: THE PROMPT IS NEVER IN ``argv``.  It is staged to a temp file and handed over as the child's stdin.
claims.why: The prompt is written to in_path and passed as stdin to ManagedProcess; argv is passed as-is.

claims.text: A file rather than a pipe because a CLI that never drains stdin deadlocks the writer OUTSIDE every timeout
claims.why: The code writes the prompt to a file and opens it for reading, not a pipe.

claims.text: on the ssh path a command-line prompt is re-parsed by the remote login shell, which turns any backtick or ``$(...)`` in a diff into remote code execution with no adversarial model required.
claims.why: This claim refers to the ssh path and behavior outside this chunk.

claims.text: The whole process TREE dies on timeout.
claims.why: The code calls proc.cancel() on timeout, but whether that kills the entire process tree depends on ManagedProcess implementation, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``args`` never contains the prompt: :attr:`stdin_prompt` is always true here and the shape is enforced by test, not by convention.
claims.why: The dataclass has stdin_prompt default True and the profiles do not include the prompt in args; enforcement by test is not visible here but the code structure supports it.

claims.text: Forbidden anywhere in a council argv.  ``workspace-write`` and ``dontAsk`` are the two flags that turn a reviewer into an agent with an editor.
claims.why: The tuple includes those fragments and _assert_profile_safe checks for them.

claims.text: Tools are named explicitly rather than allow-listing nothing: the variadic ``--allowed-tools <tools...>`` would swallow the next flag if given an empty value, so the denial is expressed with the ``=`` form, which cannot slurp.
claims.why: The profile uses `--disallowed-tools=<list>` with equals sign, not a separate argument.

claims.text: No --permission-mode at all (dontAsk is what the runtime profile carries), tools denied, MCP pinned to the empty --mcp-config set.
claims.why: The anthropic profile args do not include --permission-mode, include --disallowed-tools, and include --strict-mcp-config.

claims.text: read-only sandbox + approvals never; --skip-git-repo-check because the council cwd is a bare temp dir by design and codex otherwise refuses.
claims.why: The openai profile args include --sandbox read-only, --ask-for-approval never, and --skip-git-repo-check.

claims.text: ``ask`` is the ONLY entry point, and it always: charges the token ceiling, runs the secret floor, computes withheld paths for an untrusted lane, times the call, and maps every failure onto :data:`STATUSES`.
claims.why: The ask method is not defined in this chunk; only the class intro is present.

claims.text: A refusal is a STATUS, not an exception -- a council must never lose a participant to a traceback, because a missing turn is indistinguishable from a turn that was never sought.
claims.why: The mapping of refusals to STATUSES is not in this chunk.

observations.what: floor_check returns FloorRefusal with channel='path' if rule.startswith('secret path marker'), else 'content'. This assumes the rule string format is stable.
run_managed catches FileNotFoundError and (CancellationUnavailable, OSError) but not other exceptions; a subprocess that fails in other ways could propagate.
run_managed uses time.sleep(0.02) polling; this is a busy-wait but acceptable.
council_cwd raises ValueError if the temp dir is inside repo_root, but the docstring says 'system temp dir' – the code checks the actual temp dir, which is more precise.
COUNCIL_PROFILES is a module-level dict that is checked by _assert_profile_safe at import time; if a profile is added later, it will not be checked.
